5. In Writ Petition No. 10093 of 2013, the petitioner was the Managing Director of Hoque Food Limited and proprietor of Hoque Food Agency, the former being a limited company and the later being a proprietorship firm. In the Hoque Food Limited, the petitioner held 200 shares out of total 1,000 shares. Both Houqe Food Limited and Houqe Food Agency obtained credit facilities from the Export Import Bank of Bangladesh Limited (EXIM Bank) (respondent No.5) and the petitioner stood guarantee for the said loan by executing personal guarantee in favour of the said bank. Since both the Houqe Food Limited and Houqe Food Agency failed to repay the said loans, the Exim Bank filed Artha Rin Suit No.410 of 2004 before the concerned Artha Rin Adalat impleading the petitioner as defendant No.3. Accordingly, the said suit was decreed in favour of the bank and the bank filed Artha Execution Case No.239 of 2005 for execution of the said decree. At one stage of the execution process, the judgment-debtors including the petitioner filed application before the concerned Adalat for allowing them to repay the ,entire decreetal amount without interests by installments in view of the provisions under section 49(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Thereupon, the Adalat allowed the same and, accordingly, the debtors started repayment of installments as allowed by the Adalat. Being aggrieved by the said order of the Adalat allowing such installments without interests, the Exim Bank filed Writ Petition No. 9249 of 2010, whereupon the High Court Division issued Rule and stayed further proceedings of the said execution case. According to the petitioner, the said judgment-debtors have in the meantime paid the entire decreetal money, however, without interests. 

 8. Mr Munir Sharif, learned advocate appearing for all the petitioners, mainly submits that since the letters of guarantee concerned were executed by the petitioners before the amendment of 2013 to the definition of the term "defaulter-borrower" as provided under section 5 Ga Ga of the Bank Companies Act, 1991 ("the said Act") and the respective companies or establishments of the petitioners had become defaulters before such amendment came into force, the rights of the petitioners not to be included in the definition of 'defaulter borrower' as prevailing at the relevant time had already accrued in their favour, and, as such, in view of the provisions under section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, the amendment to the said section 5 Ga Ga inserting two more categories therein, namely 'guarantor' and 'director', will not be applicable retrospectively in respect of the petitioners. According to him, since the petitioners were not liable to be included in the definition of the 'defaulter-borrower' at the relevant time, so long as the said personal guarantees continue, no amendment inserting those categories in the said definition can take retrospective effect. In support of his submissions. Mr Sharif refers to various decisions of this Court as well as the Superior Courts of this sub-continent, namely Nazimuddin vs State, 30 DLR 49, State of Punjab vs Mohar Sings, 1955 AIR (SC) 84, Sangam Spinners vs Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I (2008) 1 SCC 291. In respect of the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 10093 of 2013, Mr Sharif submits that since pursuant to the order given by the Artha Execution Adalat, the judgment-debtors have already paid the entire decreetal money except the interests, the matter should have been resolved long ago, but through the said writ petition filed by the lender-bank the matter is still pending. Thus, he submits, the name of the petitioner should not be published in the CIB report anymore. However, in respect of Writ Petition No. 9158 of 2012 and Writ Petition No. 10093 of 2013, Mr Sharif frankly concedes that the arguments as to the retrospective effect of the amendment to section 5 GaGa of the said Act is not applicable in respect of the petitioners in those writ petitions as admittedly the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 9158 of 2012 held more then 20% shares in Mystic bringing him even under the un- amended definition of the 'defaulter-borrower' and the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 10093 of 20iJ, being proprietor of Hoque Food Agency, was also liable to be included in the said un- amended definition of 'defaulter-borrower' even before the said amendment. Further, referring to the larger Bench decision of this Court in Quazi Nasibul Hassan vs Bangladesh Bank, 61 DLR 96, Mr Sharif argues that the issue whether the guarantor would be included in the definition of 'defaulter-borrower' having already been settled by a decision of a larger Bench of this Court holding that the guarantors would not be included in the said un-amended definition of 'defaulter-borrower', they were not liable to be referred to the Bangladesh Bank under section 27 KaKa of the said Act for publication of their names in the CIB. This being so, he continues, unless the amendment to section 5 GaGa of the said Act is applied retrospectively to the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 10472 of 2012, the petitioner's name cannot be published in the CIB report of Bangladesh Bank as, though he was a Director, he was holding only 10% shares in the borrower company and executed personal guarantee. But, he submits, by inclusion of the word 'director' in the definition of defaulter-borrower' by the said amendment, he is now affected on both counts, namely as 'director' and as 'guarantor'.
